subject: general
question: Which of the following best defines an ion?

options.text: An atom with equal number of protons and electrons
A molecule with more neutrons than protons
A neutral particle formed by the combination of atoms
An atom or group of atoms that has a positive or negative charge

solution:
The correct answer is __**An atom or group of atoms that has a positive or negative charge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An ion** is defined as an **atom or a group of atoms** that has gained or lost electrons, resulting in a net positive or negative charge.
 
• Ions are classified into two types: **Cations** (positive charge) and **Anions** (negative charge). Cations are formed when atoms lose electrons, while anions are formed when atoms gain electrons.
 
• The charge of an ion is determined by the difference between the number of **protons (positively charged particles)** and **electrons (negatively charged particles)** present in the atom or molecule.
 
• Ions play a vital role in several scientific and industrial processes, including **chemical bonding, electrical conductivity, and biological functions**.
 
• The term "ion" was introduced by **Michael Faraday** in 1834, derived from the Greek word "ienai," meaning "to go," indicating the movement of charged particles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Cations:**

 
 
• Cations are positively charged ions formed when an atom loses electrons.
 
• They are smaller in size compared to their parent atom due to the loss of electrons and reduced electron-electron repulsion.
 
• Examples include **Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺, and Al³⁺**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Anions:**
 
 
• Anions are negatively charged ions formed when an atom gains electrons.
 
• They are larger in size compared to their parent atom due to the addition of electrons and increased electron-electron repulsion.
 
• Examples include **Cl⁻, OH⁻, NO₃⁻, and SO₄²⁻**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Ions:**
 
 
• Ions are essential for biological processes like **nerve impulse transmission, muscle contraction, and maintaining fluid balance**.
 
• They are vital in industrial applications such as **batteries, electroplating, and water purification**.
 
• In chemical reactions, ions participate in processes like **acid-base reactions and ionic bonding**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Common Ionic Compounds:**
 
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)**: Composed of Na⁺ and Cl⁻.
 
• **Magnesium oxide (MgO)**: Composed of Mg²⁺ and O²⁻.
 
• **Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)**: Contains Ca²⁺ and CO₃²⁻.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relation with Electricity:**

 
 
• In solutions, ions are responsible for **conducting electricity**. For example, electrolytes in water enable current flow.
 
• In solid-state physics, ionic crystals exhibit unique properties due to the arrangement of ions.
 
 
 
• **Formation of Ions in Nature:**
 
 
• Ions are naturally formed during phenomena like **lightning**, where air molecules become ionized.
 
• **Solar radiation** causes ionization in the Earth's atmosphere, creating the ionosphere, which impacts radio wave propagation.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Medicine:**
 
 
• **Electrolyte imbalance** in the human body is diagnosed and treated based on ion concentrations like Na⁺, K⁺, and Cl⁻.
 
• Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) play a critical role in **bone strength and enzymatic processes**.
